title: Four seeds, one in four each
hook: Each seed has a 1 in 4 chance of a white flower. How likely is a white one among four?

knows: offspring get one copy of a gene from each parent
a recessive trait shows only with two copies
doesNotKnow: that a Mendelian ratio is a chance per offspring
how chances combine across several independent offspring

misconception: If two carriers have 4 offspring, exactly one will show the recessive trait (1 in 4 is a quota).
objective: The learner can explain that a 1 in 4 chance applies to each offspring separately, so in families of 4 the number with the trait varies, and the chance of at least one is 1 - (3/4)^4, about 68%.

claims.text: When two carriers (one dominant and one recessive copy each) breed, each offspring gets one copy from each parent with equal chance, so it has two recessive copies with chance 1/4, independently of its siblings.
claims.source: Mendel's law of segregation; Griffiths et al., Introduction to Genetic Analysis (W. H. Freeman), chapter on single-gene inheritance.

claims.text: With 4 independent seeds at 1/4 each, each seed is purple with chance 3/4, so all four are purple with chance 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 x 3/4 = 81/256, about 32% (the stage shows this product beside the count of families with none white), so at least one is white with chance about 68%.
Exactly one white of four happens in only about 42% of families on average (the learner sees their own count of 100); about a third get none (32%) and about a quarter get two or more (26%).

The 100 families on the stage are one fixed seeded random field (seed 1, chosen without tuning the counts); the counts the learner sees (67 with a white flower, 49 with exactly one) vary from field to field around the expected 68 and 42.
claims.source: Demo.tsx batch(): two fair allele draws per seed with a seeded PRNG; 'New field' changes the seed.

claims.text: The flower is made up: one purple copy (P) is enough for purple (complete dominance), and seeds are independent.
claims.source: Modelling choice stated in the reveal.

recall.question: Each child of two carriers has a 1 in 4 chance of a recessive trait. They have 2 children. What is the chance that neither has it?
recall.why: Each child independently escapes with chance 3/4, so both do with chance 3/4 x 3/4 = 9/16, about 56%.
